evals.prompt: Build a small React synth: one oscillator through a lowpass filter and a gain. The UI has a volume slider, a cutoff slider, and a 'Sweep' button that ramps the cutoff from its current value up to 12 kHz and back over 2 seconds. Use @audiorective/core and @audiorective/react. Write the audio class, the engine module, and the React components as separate files. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A Synth AudioProcessor subclass owning the nodes, an engine module using createEngine, and React components that read params with useValue and call a sweep method
expectations: Defines a class that extends AudioProcessor from @audiorective/core
Constructs the audio nodes as local variables before calling super() and binds params to AudioParams via bind
Exposes a getter named output on the processor
The filter sweep (setValueAtTime / linearRampToValueAtTime against currentTime) is implemented as a method on the processor class, not inside a React component or hook
The React button handler only calls the processor method (no scheduling code in the component)
Uses useValue to read a param in a React component and writes back with param.value = ...
Creates the engine with createEngine and exposes EngineProvider/useEngine via createEngineContext
Does not import or use Tone.js
Does not use a separate state store (Redux, Zustand, React useState) to mirror audio parameter values

evals.prompt: We're adding an audio workspace to a Next.js 15 app (app router). The engine module is at app/studio/audio/engine.ts and exports `engine` created with createEngine from @audiorective/core. Right now `next build` fails with EngineEnvironmentError. Show me the file layout and code changes that fix this properly. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A client-only boundary (next/dynamic with ssr: false) around the audio subtree, with the engine module only imported from inside it
expectations: Uses next/dynamic with ssr: false (or an equivalent client-only boundary) to mount the audio subtree
Keeps createEngine at module scope inside the client-only subtree rather than making it lazy or nullable
Explains that 'use client' alone does not prevent server evaluation
Does not recommend a typeof window guard, a nullable engine, or a lazy getter as the fix
Identifies that the fix is to move the import path that reaches the engine module inside the boundary

evals.prompt: Write a 16-step drum machine (kick, snare, hat) in TypeScript with @audiorective/core and @audiorective/clock. It needs start/stop, a BPM control, and toggling steps while it's playing. Samples are at /kit/kick.wav, /kit/snare.wav, /kit/hat.wav. Vanilla TS with a minimal DOM UI is fine. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A DrumMachine processor that uses the clock's look-ahead tick windows to schedule Sampler triggers, with the step pattern in a Cell and the UI only toggling and reading state
expectations: Uses @audiorective/clock for transport and tempo rather than setInterval or a hand-rolled scheduler
Uses Sampler (or another audiorective playback primitive) for the one-shot drum hits
Stores the step pattern as a Cell (or in a plain class holding a Cell), not as a Param<boolean[][]> and not in DOM state
Schedules hits from the clock's tick windows / rulers with audio-time timestamps, not on the main thread at playback time
Keeps scheduling logic in the audio class; DOM handlers only call methods like toggleStep / start / stop
Resumes or starts the AudioContext from a user gesture

evals.prompt: In our audiorective project, calling `sampler.params.mute.value = true` throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading value)'. The docs you have say Sampler has a mute param. What's going on and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses a version mismatch between the installed @audiorective/core and the documented API, checks the changelog and the installed version, and recommends upgrading
expectations: Suspects the installed package predates the documented API rather than assuming the docs are wrong
Consults the changelog reference to find which version added Sampler.params.mute
Checks the installed version via node_modules/@audiorective/core/package.json or an equivalent command
Recommends upgrading the @audiorective/* packages together instead of hand-rolling a mute gain node

evals.prompt: Build a vanilla TypeScript clip selector with @audiorective/widgets. My app supplies an AudioContext and a gain node for the output; do not create or close a context inside the widget integration. Load /audio/loop.wav, support replacing it with a File, select 1–2 seconds programmatically, show loading errors, and clean up on unmount. Explain which interactions start audition. Use the current workspace package if this API is Unreleased. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: A mountWaveformSelector integration using a caller-owned context and routed output, asynchronous readiness and recovery, and explicit lifecycle cleanup.
expectations: Imports mountWaveformSelector from @audiorective/widgets and supplies the existing context in options
Connects handle.output to the supplied gain node and does not automatically bypass that chain with a destination connection
Awaits or catches handle.ready and uses handle.load(file) for replacement; catches loading failures or reads getState().error
Calls setSelection({ start: 1, end: 2 }) only after confirming at least 2 seconds of loaded duration
Uses getState() fields including loading or error rather than inventing a subscribe/onStateChange API
Destroys the selector on unmount and leaves the caller context open
Explains that pointer selection creation and pointer handle resize audition/loop, clicking seeks/plays, and keyboard or programmatic metadata changes do not start a stopped player
Does not introduce WaveSurfer, React bindings, or a generic preset/plugin framework
Identifies that Unreleased APIs need a workspace build or packed artifact instead of claiming npm @latest includes them

evals.prompt: Use only @audiorective/widgets/waveform in vanilla TypeScript to display supplied Float32Array peaks for a 6-second clip. Add metadata-only selection and a custom marker at 2 seconds that tracks zoom/data changes. Feed an external playhead position. No audio context, node, player, or framework. Show cleanup and implement the marker only through public plugin APIs. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: An audio-independent mountWaveform view with createSelectionPlugin, externally supplied playhead, and a WaveformPlugin using attachment-owned overlays and subscriptions.
expectations: Imports mountWaveform, createSelectionPlugin, and WaveformPlugin types from @audiorective/widgets/waveform only
Provides data as { peaks: Float32Array, duration: 6 } and feeds position with setPlayhead
Attaches the selection plugin before calling its setSelection and treats change/commit callbacks as metadata only
Creates no AudioContext, audio nodes, engine, or audio player and never starts audio in selection callbacks
Implements the marker as attach(context), mounts its overlay with context.mountOverlay, and positions it with context.timeToX(2)
Subscribes through context.onViewportChange and context.onDataChange so marker position tracks geometry and data changes
Uses attachment-owned resource helpers or context.onCleanup for added resources; calls attachment.destroy or view.destroy to clean up
Uses no private DOM queries, ar- class selectors, test ids, deep imports, or patching of widget internals

evals.prompt: Use @audiorective/widgets/waveform to display a six-second clip with a custom SVG or Canvas waveform drawing, not a plugin overlay on the default waveform. Retain metadata selection, beat snapping, zoom, and an external playhead. Use the public renderer option, handle data clearing and resize, and clean up resources. Also show how the same renderer is passed to the complete mountWaveformSelector with a caller-owned AudioContext. Use the workspace build for this Unreleased API. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: A WaveformRenderer factory passed to the renderer option, with actual custom drawing and an instance render/destroy lifecycle; widget owns timeline and selection.
expectations: Uses public WaveformRenderer and passes renderer to mountWaveform, without hiding/querying the default drawing or using a plugin to cover it
Mounts custom SVG, Canvas, or DOM once in the supplied container and returns an object with render(frame) and optional destroy()
Draws from frame.peaks.min/max and width/height, handles null peaks by clearing, and treats peak arrays as read-only
Uses full content CSS-pixel dimensions and preserves the linear time axis; Canvas examples manage their own backing resolution
Attaches createSelectionPlugin with a supplied beat grid and snap mode; feeds external position through setPlayhead without creating audio in the pure view
Releases additional resources in destroy and lets the widget handle redraws for zoom, resize, and source replacement
Passes the same factory via renderer to mountWaveformSelector, with the caller supplying the AudioContext and routing output
Introduces no new renderer package, React binding, WaveSurfer dependency, or audio editing state in the renderer

evals.prompt: Use the current Audiorective workspace build to load one audio File into a headless block, then attach two waveform selectors sharing selection and playback. Use one caller-owned AudioContext and output gain chain, distinct renderers and beat snapping, and allow either view to be unmounted while audition continues. Show headless selection/audition, source replacement, error handling and final cleanup. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: WavePlayer from @audiorective/blocks owns audio and selection; two mountWaveformSelector calls receive the same player; cleanup respects borrowed ownership.
expectations: Imports WavePlayer from @audiorective/blocks; awaits player.load and catches current load failures
Routes player.output to the caller gain once; creates or closes no context inside the integration
Passes the same player to both mountWaveformSelector calls, without context or a second player
Uses player.setSelection and player.audition for headless operation instead of synthesizing DOM gestures
Uses renderer and grid options per view without mirroring selection into a separate store
Destroying one view leaves player and peer usable; final cleanup destroys both views then player
Uses documented subscribe for non-clock changes and reads position on animation frames if a custom playhead is needed
Does not invent destructive PCM editing; optional stretch requires an injected processor; APIs under Unreleased require a workspace build

evals.prompt: Build a full pitch-preserving time-stretch waveform selector with the current Audiorective workspace packages. Host supplies AudioContext, output gain and a compiled compatible Rubber Band WebAssembly.Module. Load a File, use two shared selectors with SVG/Canvas and source beat snapping, preserve original PCM, render from original for each ratio, show pending/errors, keep waveform/audio same revision, audition the output selection, handle stale jobs and cleanup without closing context. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: TimeStretch from pure effects/time-stretch is injected into WavePlayer; setStretch commits a complete buffer/peaks version consumed by both selectors.
expectations: Uses new TimeStretch(module) from @audiorective/effects/time-stretch with caller-supplied WASM, without bundling a GPL binary or inventing a default WASM URL
Injects the processor via new WavePlayer(context, {stretch}) and connects player.output to the caller gain once
Mounts two selectors with the same player, separate renderers and source-coordinate grids
Awaits player.load before editing and calls player.setStretch(ratio) rather than rebuilding transport or rewriting original PCM
Uses committed stretchRatio/duration/revision and processing/error state; pending render keeps the previous version usable
Treats successful stretch as a stopped commit with selection/position mapped into output seconds; sourceToOutput/outputToSource can convert coordinates
Uses player.version.peaks as the committed summary and lets the selector share it; standalone PCM summaries use core/peaks and have no display normalization
Handles newer edit/source load replacing older work without publishing stale results; does not mirror buffers/selection into UI stores
Destroys views then player then borrowed TimeStretch, leaving context and caller gain chain alive
Uses workspace/packed artifacts for Unreleased APIs and does not claim seamless live warp or sample-accurate dynamic stretch

evals.prompt: Build a vanilla TypeScript waveform selector for a caller-owned AudioContext. Show download bytes and a progress bar only when the total is known, indeterminate feedback for decode/peaks, a cancel button, and retry after cancellation or failure. Two views must observe the same state. We already have a URL-to-AudioBuffer cache: integrate it without a second loading store or a second decode; cancelling this observer must not cancel other cache readers. Use Audiorective public APIs, provide cleanup and do not fake percentages.
evals.expected_output: A shared WavePlayer with loadSource URL cache adapter, state snapshots/subscriptions and cancelLoad, plus selectors or custom feedback observing the same player. The adapter detaches on abort/settle while the shared job can continue.
expectations: Uses WavePlayer loading and loadProgress through getState()/subscribe(), rendering an initial snapshot because subscribe is not immediate.
Uses download/read loadedBytes and totalBytes; null or nonpositive totals and decode/peaks are indeterminate, with no fake percentage.
Both views share one player and see the same progress/cancellation; UI does not independently track audio loading.
Calls cancelLoad() and retries with load(); treats current errors separately from superseded/cancelled loads.
Provides a loadSource URL adapter using context, signal and onProgress with Promise<AudioBuffer>; reuses the decoded cache instead of decoding a second time.
The cache adapter removes progress/abort listeners when cancelled or settled while protecting other readers.
Loading another source or destroying the block cannot publish stale progress or decoded results.
Cleans up observers and views before destroying the app-owned player, and leaves the caller-owned context open.

evals.prompt: Use current Audiorective workspace packages to inspect an SMF File in two piano rolls with shared time selection and source-tempo snapping. Use different note drawings, a pitch/velocity inspector, external playhead, and an existing caller-owned synth. Include invalid file recovery, one-view removal and final cleanup. Do not create a MIDI device connection or a new synth/transport in the widget.
evals.expected_output: MidiSequence and MIDI utilities from @audiorective/midi own note data and selection. mountPianoRoll from widgets/piano-roll borrows the same model; custom renderer changes note drawing while caller instruments and audio scheduling remain independent.
expectations: Imports MidiSequence/midiGrid from @audiorective/midi and mountPianoRoll from @audiorective/widgets/piano-roll, using a workspace build for Unreleased APIs.
Awaits File.arrayBuffer before synchronous sequence.load, guards stale reads, and catches parse failures without replacing the previous snapshot.
Uses source tempo/signature metadata via midiGrid rather than assuming a constant120 BPM.
Both views borrow one sequence; note edits go through updateNote and selection through the shared model without mirrored audio/UI state.
Renderer uses frame timeToX/pitchToY and visible spanning notes; view has no AudioContext, synth or device permissions.
Note inspection calls caller controls; read-only inspection omits onNoteEdit and does not promise lossless SMF export, pedal/controller rendering or Web MIDI I/O.
Caller clips sustained notes to audition bounds, schedules its instrument and cancels active/future voices on pause/seek/source replacement/edit/destroy.
Removing one view preserves peer/model/audio; final cleanup destroys views, caller audio and sequence independently.

evals.prompt: Use current Audiorective workspace packages to add a custom cue marker and pointer interaction to two piano rolls that borrow one existing MIDI model. The same time-based plugin factory must work on a waveform too. Keep the default note renderer and caller audio. Follow zoom, horizontal scroll, resizing and source replacement. Support detaching one marker independently and final view cleanup. Use only public APIs; no internal DOM selectors or assumed keyboard offsets.
evals.expected_output: A WaveformPlugin mounted through PianoRollHandle.attach and WaveformHandle.attach, using the supplied shared context for source-second coordinates, overlays, subscriptions and cleanup.
expectations: Imports mountPianoRoll and WaveformPlugin/WaveformPluginContext from the public piano-roll entry, with workspace/packed artifacts for Unreleased APIs.
Uses view.attach(plugin) and its returned PluginAttachment; keeps note drawing in the default renderer rather than replacing it to obtain coordinates.
Uses ctx.timeToX and ctx.clientXToTime, public surface/getViewport/getViewportRect, with no private DOM selectors or hard-coded keyboard offsets.
Mounts overlay through ctx.mountOverlay, draws initially, and updates through ctx.onViewportChange and ctx.onDataChange; observes borrowed model separately for selection-only changes.
An interactive overlay child opts into pointer-events and stops pointerdown propagation when appropriate to preserve native selection ownership.
Uses ctx.listen/onCleanup for owned resources; detaching one plugin removes its overlay/listeners/subscriptions while peer/model/audio remain alive.
Reuses a plugin factory for waveform and piano-roll without pretending the time context exposes pitch editing or a second selection owner.
Final cleanup destroys view attachments without destroying a borrowed model or caller audio; no extra AudioContext, player or mirrored note store.

evals.prompt: Use current Audiorective workspace packages to build two piano rolls sharing our existing MidiSequence. Give the second one a custom right-side keyboard, bottom toolbar and SVG note shapes. Its snap control must reflect the initial option and later handle.setSnap calls from outside the layout. Both must support widget-owned note move and edge-resize with beat snap/Alt bypass, local drag previews and one model commit on release. Preserve range selection, inspection, external audio ownership and cancel edits on Escape/source replacement/unmount. Provide cleanup; do not implement another drag engine in the renderer.
evals.expected_output: mountPianoRoll layout and renderer change appearance while forwarding pointerdown to widget editing; onNoteEdit invokes the existing model command.
expectations: Uses layout(root, viewport, controls) and mounts the supplied viewport unchanged inside root, with public frame geometry and control methods.

Reads layout frame.snap to initialize and refresh the custom snap control, writes changes through controls.setSnap, and relies on synchronous layout updates for external handle.setSnap calls without another snap store.
Layouts/renderers return render and optional destroy, manage owned listeners/resources and responsive controls, without private DOM selectors.
Enables onNoteEdit and updates the borrowed sequence with edited note start/end/pitch; leaves audio scheduling/routing with the caller.
Custom note renderer forwards onNotePointerDown(note,event,optionalKind), retains onNoteClick/keyboard inspection, and does not implement capture/delta/snap itself.
Uses widget snap/grid controls and Alt bypass, retains local-only preview plus single synchronous pointer-release command, and does not mirror durable notes.
Documents cancellation on Escape, pointercancel, source/geometry replacement and destruction, preserving peer/model/audio lifetime.
Keeps background range selection separate from note editing and does not promise auto-scroll, multi-note editing or lossless SMF export.

evals.prompt: Use the workspace build of @audiorective to add a source-time gain envelope to a non-looping waveform selection. The audio owner already has a WavePlayer, whose output is time-stretched to twice its source duration. Another view may change selection or stretch while play() awaits AudioContext.resume(). Use the optional core automation entry, schedule the selected range and allow live curve replacement. Show stop, manual control takeover and destroy. Also explain how a multi-target Rack macro would adapt without putting Rack knowledge in core. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: An audio owner borrows WavePlayer and owns a curve and finite AutomationBinding through an explicit native target; WavePlayer attaches the binding and handles source/output mapping, shared start, and pending edits.
expectations: Imports AutomationCurve, AutomationBinding and audioParamTarget from @audiorective/core/automation, not the root barrel
Uses outgoing linear/hold shapes and replaces curve.value for validated edits; raw curve.$ writes require a valid sorted immutable snapshot
Passes a native AudioParam (such as params.gain.audioParam) to audioParamTarget, not plain Param or a macro subclass
Uses player.attachSourceAutomation(binding) so WavePlayer maps output selection and stretch ratio into source-time binding coordinates
Keeps scheduling and lifetime in an audio owner; widget callbacks call methods or change the shared curve
Detaches or stops binding before manual native AudioParam or SchedulableParam value assignment, target replacement or processor destruction
Does not implement setInterval/rAF scheduling, copy the scheduler, or claim the binding changes PCM/peaks
Explains AutomationTarget.program receives relative seconds plus absolute when; hold cancels and preserves the value at the supplied absolute audio time
Keeps Rack macro resolution and nonlinear fanout in a block/app adapter; does not use the macro native backing as a substitute
Distinguishes planned curve sampling from existing native ParamSync readback, including disconnected-node limitations
Starts the player with player.play({ when }) using a lookahead on the audio clock; the attachment shares the effective start time and no binding starts when play resolves null
Lets the attachment invalidate pending playback on selection or stretch edits; does not add an app-owned operation token or copy the selection/time mapping

evals.prompt: In a React app that already has a shared WavePlayer and a MidiSequence, build a small status bar that shows 'Loading...' with the byte progress while the player loads, the current selection in seconds, the stretch 'Rendering...' flag and any error, plus the number of MIDI notes. It must update live with no polling and no copying of player state into a store. Also add a button that clears the selection. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: React components that read player.cells.* and sequence.cells.* with useValue, and call owner methods for writes
expectations: Reads WavePlayer state through player.cells (selection, loading, loadProgress, processing, error) with useValue, not by copying getState() into useState or a store, and not by polling
Reads the MIDI note count through sequence.cells.notes (or cells.state) with useValue
Clears the selection by calling player.setSelection(null); does not assign to player.cells.selection.value or call its $ with a value
Reads position per animation frame from the player.position getter rather than trying to observe it as a reactive value
Does not call subscribe in the components for state that player.cells exposes

evals.prompt: build me a 16-step drum machine in react with a bpm slider, swing, and per-step velocity. the kit is 4 wav files in public/kit/. don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: An audio-layer class schedules one-shot hits from the clock's look-ahead windows; the pattern and velocities are reactive state the React UI reads and edits directly. Any equivalent wiring of the same primitives is acceptable.
expectations: Chooses the timing primitive from @audiorective/clock (Clock/Timeline tick windows or rulers) for transport, tempo and swing, rather than setInterval, setTimeout or requestAnimationFrame scheduling

Chooses a one-shot playback primitive from @audiorective/core (Sampler/Voice, or an equivalent buffer source scheduled with audio-clock times) for the hits, with per-step velocity applied as gain at trigger time
Does not import a step-sequencer, drum-machine or sample-bank class from @audiorective/blocks or @audiorective/widgets; none exists, so the sequencing logic is written in the app's audio layer

Keeps pattern and velocity in reactive state owned by the audio layer (a Cell, or a plain class holding Cells) and reads it in React with useValue; no second copy of the pattern in useState, a context or an external store
Scheduling lives in an audio-layer class or method; React handlers only write params/cells or call methods
Adds no wrapper layer around the library's primitives that only forwards calls (no re-implemented transport, event bus or subscription system)

evals.prompt: sampler pad grid: 8 pads, each plays a one-shot, polyphonic, with a fade out on release. vanilla TS, no framework. don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Pads trigger polyphonic voices from core's Sampler (or an equivalent per-pad voice primitive); releasing a pad fades that pad's own voice. Equivalent wiring is acceptable.
expectations: Chooses core's Sampler/Voice (or an equivalent polyphonic one-shot primitive from @audiorective/core) for playback, one voice per press
Does not use WavePlayer, mountWaveformSelector or BufferPlayer as the pad voice: they are single-playhead players and cannot overlap hits of the same pad
Release fades the voice that this press started, using the voice's own fade/stop with a release time (or an equivalent scheduled gain ramp), so overlapping presses release independently
Keeps independent one-shot pads on core Sampler/Voice; InstrumentEvents is for cancellable grouped choke, which this request does not need
Triggering goes through a method on the audio-layer object; pointer and keyboard handlers do not create audio nodes themselves
Starts or resumes the AudioContext from a user gesture

evals.prompt: replace tone.js in our looper — we only use Tone.Transport, Tone.Player and a PingPongDelay and the bundle is huge. show me the audiorective equivalent of each and how they connect. don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Transport maps to @audiorective/clock, the loop player to a core playback primitive with a scheduled start, and the delay to @audiorective/effects PingPongDelay, wired with defineGraph or plain connections.
expectations: Maps Tone.Transport to @audiorective/clock (transport, tempo, look-ahead scheduling) rather than a hand-rolled timer
Maps Tone.Player to a playback primitive whose start can be scheduled on the audio clock (BufferPlayer, or WavePlayer/Sampler with a stated reason), and says why that one fits a tempo-locked loop
Uses PingPongDelay from @audiorective/effects instead of rebuilding it from DelayNodes
Connects source to effect to destination through defineGraph or the processors' input/output nodes
Does not introduce a compatibility wrapper that re-creates Tone's API on top of audiorective
Starts loops from clock tick windows or an explicit audio-clock time, not from the main thread at playback time

evals.prompt: I need a browser waveform editor in vanilla TypeScript: load a local audio file, drag a time range, and loop audition that selection. I already have an AudioContext and an effects chain it should play through. don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Uses the waveform selector widget (or the waveform view plus a WavePlayer) with the caller's AudioContext, routing the player's output into the existing chain.
expectations: Chooses the existing waveform capability: mountWaveformSelector from @audiorective/widgets, or mountWaveform with a WavePlayer from @audiorective/blocks; does not hand-draw peaks on a canvas or write its own range-drag logic
Passes the caller's AudioContext (or a caller-owned WavePlayer) rather than creating a second AudioContext
Routes the player/selector output into the existing effects chain once, instead of connecting straight to the destination
Loads the File through the widget or player's load, and handles a failed load
Loop audition of the selection uses the player's own selection/looping/audition methods, not a re-implemented loop with AudioBufferSourceNode
Cleans up on unmount without closing the caller's AudioContext

evals.prompt: I want a granular texture player on top of our audiorective setup: load one sample, then continuously scatter 30–80 ms grains from random positions in it, heavily overlapping, each grain with its own pan and pitch jitter, plus a density slider and a position-spread slider. don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: A custom AudioProcessor that schedules many short overlapping grain sources on the audio clock, with density and spread as params. The single-playhead blocks are not a fit and are not used for the grains.
expectations: Does not use WavePlayer (or mountWaveformSelector) to play grains: it has one playhead and one selection, so it cannot overlap dozens of grains
Builds the grain engine as an AudioProcessor subclass (or an equivalent audio-layer class) that owns its nodes and exposes an output

Each grain is its own short-lived source (Sampler/Voice triggers with offset, rate and duration, or raw AudioBufferSourceNode + gain envelope + panner) started with audio-clock times, so grains overlap
Grain start times are scheduled ahead on the audio clock (a clock tick window or an equivalent look-ahead loop), not fired from the main thread at playback time
Density and spread are reactive params/cells on the processor that the UI writes directly
May use loadAudioBuffer, Param/Cell and effects from the library; reaching below the blocks to core is the expected choice here and is not treated as a failure to use the library

evals.prompt: Hook up live Web MIDI input in our audiorective app: a keyboard plays our polyphonic synth with note on/off and velocity, the sustain pedal holds notes, and the UI lights up the keys that are currently held. don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Web MIDI messages are handled directly and call methods on the synth's audio-layer object; held notes are reactive state. MidiSequence and the SMF parser are not used for live input.
expectations: Does not route live note-on/note-off through MidiSequence or parseMidi: they hold and edit note data from MIDI files in source seconds, not a live input stream
Does not mount the piano-roll widget as the live keyboard display unless it is fed by state the app owns for that purpose and the answer says why
Handles navigator.requestMIDIAccess and message parsing in app code, calling noteOn/noteOff-style methods on an AudioProcessor synth
Sustain pedal logic (deferring releases while the pedal is down) lives in the audio-layer object, not in UI handlers
Held notes are a Cell (or equivalent reactive state on the audio-layer object) that the UI observes; no duplicate copy in a UI store
Says plainly that MidiRecorder writes takes but does not route live keyboard events to a synth; core primitives remain the right level for playing

evals.prompt: Add a simple podcast player bar to our audiorective app: play/pause, a seek slider, elapsed and total time, and a 1x/1.5x/2x speed toggle. Episodes are 60–90 minute mp3s on our CDN. No waveform. vanilla TS. don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Uses core's streaming FilePlayer with the plain player widget for play/pause, seek and time; adds a small app-owned playback-rate control. The waveform selector and WavePlayer are not used because they decode the whole file.
expectations: Chooses FilePlayer from @audiorective/core for the episode, because it streams instead of decoding the whole file
Does not use WavePlayer, mountWaveformSelector or BufferPlayer for a 60–90 minute file, and if it mentions them says they decode the entire file into memory
Mounts the plain player widget from @audiorective/widgets/player with fromFilePlayer(player) for play/pause, seek and time, rather than rebuilding those controls
Relies on the widget to handle unknown duration and hold the seek slider against incoming time updates during a drag
Keeps the FilePlayer caller-owned: routes its output once and destroys the view separately from the player
Speed changes go through the player's playbackRate; play is started from a user gesture

evals.prompt: Our audiorective step sequencer schedules open and closed hi-hats ahead through Clock. If I delete a future closed-hat step, its voice stops but the previously scheduled choke still mutes the open hat. An edit may also land exactly at a hit's AudioContext start time. A manually pressed open hat must survive sequencer pause and edits. Show the audio owner and Clock callback, plus what happens on edit, stop and cleanup. Don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: InstrumentEvents owns reversible grouped choke; Clock owns only sequenced event handles registered with window.own(hit, when), and refreshes owned hits at or after the captured audio time while manual hits stay unregistered.
expectations: Chooses InstrumentEvents from @audiorective/blocks for grouped sample hits instead of scheduling an irreversible Voice.stop(when) on the open hat
Creates open and closed pads with different IDs in one group; routes the block output once and keeps context ownership with the caller
Schedules a hit in a Clock tick window using absolute point.time and registers its returned handle with window.own(hit, point.time)
Leaves a manually triggered pad event unregistered with Clock so sequencer transport changes do not cancel it

After a pattern edit, calls clock.refresh() to retract owned hits at or after the captured audio time and refill the horizon; explains that a hit exactly at now is reissued once while earlier hits remain active
Explains that pause, stop, seek, start and destroy cancel owned events, while unowned events retain Clock's prior tail behavior
Destroys Clock and InstrumentEvents separately; the caller closes its AudioContext

evals.prompt: Make a vanilla TypeScript game soundboard: each button plays a short independent one-shot sound, and rapid clicks may overlap. There are no choke groups, step edits or transport. Use our audiorective packages; don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Core Sampler/Voice handles independent overlapping one-shots; no Clock or InstrumentEvents block is needed.
expectations: Chooses core Sampler or Voice for overlapping one-shot playback
Does not add Clock, an event-ownership registry or InstrumentEvents because there is no future choke or editable sequencer
Routes the sampler output once and starts the AudioContext from a user gesture
Keeps soundboard button callbacks thin; audio scheduling and voice lifetime stay with the audio owner

evals.prompt: Build a browser voice-track capture flow with the workspace audiorective packages. A metronome is already playing from our AudioContext. Record a short microphone take beginning at a scheduled audio-clock time, stop it from a button, then hand the PCM and its raw position to our future clip owner. The microphone and monitoring belong to the app. Show cancellation and cleanup; do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: AudioRecorder borrows the app's AudioContext and microphone input, captures PCM through a scheduled AudioWorklet take, and returns actual sample-frame timing without inventing a Track or applying an unmeasured latency correction.
expectations: Imports AudioRecorder from @audiorective/blocks and constructs it with the existing AudioContext
Obtains microphone permission in the app, connects its MediaStreamAudioSourceNode to recorder.input, and does not expect an audible recorder output
Awaits recorder.ready before a precise scheduled start, then awaits recorder.start({ when }) with absolute AudioContext seconds
Uses recorder.stop() to obtain channels, sampleRate, startFrame/endFrame or startTime/endTime; the stop button handles rejection
Treats returned frame positions as actual raw capture times and leaves latency calibration and take placement to the future clip/track owner
Uses recorder.cancel() for discard and destroys the recorder separately from the borrowed stream and AudioContext
Does not use MediaRecorder timeslice count as a sample-accurate timeline or invent a project-wide recording/track model

evals.prompt: Build a browser MIDI take recorder with the workspace audiorective packages. We already have a playing metronome, AudioContext, and polyphonic synth. The user picks one Web MIDI keyboard, presses record before the next bar, plays overlapping notes and the sustain pedal, then stops. Hand the resulting notes and their raw position to our future clip owner and show them in a piano roll. Keep live keyboard playback and permission in our app; show cancel and cleanup. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: MidiRecorder borrows the selected MIDIInput and AudioContext, captures raw timestamped messages and take-relative note data, while MidiSequence displays the take and the caller owns live synth routing and clip placement.
expectations: Obtains Web MIDI permission and selects MIDIInput in app code; constructs MidiRecorder from @audiorective/midi/web with the existing AudioContext and selected input
Resumes the context, starts with recorder.start({ when }) in absolute AudioContext seconds, then calls synchronous recorder.stop() when the take ends
Uses take.notes and take.duration with MidiSequence or a compatible piano-roll model, and passes absolute take.startTime/endTime to the future clip owner
Understands take.events preserves controllers including sustain while note projection ends at key release; does not claim sustain automatically extends notes
Keeps keyboard-to-synth noteOn/noteOff and sustain playback in the app's audio owner, separate from the recorder and piano-roll view
Uses recorder.cancel() to discard, recorder.destroy() for listener cleanup, and leaves the borrowed MIDI input and AudioContext owned by the app
Does not invent a Track/Clip owner, apply unmeasured latency correction, or treat mapped MIDI event times as sample accurate

evals.prompt: We recorded a MIDI keyboard take with the audiorective MidiRecorder, including overlapping same-pitch notes and sustain pedal messages. The user changes one note's pitch in the piano roll and wants to hear the edited take. Show how to prepare the events for our existing synth scheduler. At the same timestamp, a note release and pedal-down arrived in a particular order; preserve it. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Compiles the current MidiSequence notes with the recorded take's non-note messages using compileMidiPlaybackEvents, preserving recorded ties and note identity while leaving playback scheduling to the app.
expectations: Imports compileMidiPlaybackEvents and MidiSequence from @audiorective/midi, and constructs or updates a sequence from the recorded take
Calls compileMidiPlaybackEvents(take, sequence.getState()) after the note edit, rather than sending raw take.events alongside edited notes
Explains that matched raw note messages carry noteId, so edited pitch/timing regenerates note bytes while overlapping notes retain distinct identities
Explains that non-note messages including sustain remain and same-time original delivery order is retained; new note endpoints use the documented deterministic order
Treats returned event.time as take-relative seconds and leaves clip placement, synth scheduling, transport cancellation and live keyboard routing with the application
Does not invent a public MidiPlayer, claim MidiSequence itself stores controllers, or claim the compiler implements pedal sound behavior
